scenes.text: What if every camera on your street could help bring a lost dog home, without anyone scrubbing through hours of footage?
Today, that means knocking on doors, posting in group chats, and asking neighbours to rewind video. Ring can search Ring cameras. Most streets have a mix.
This is Find My Dog. It searches footage from any camera, for any pet, with the owner in control. Here's the real app, running live.
I'm starting a brand-new report on the deployed site. The health check reports real models, not mock mode, and nothing is preloaded.
I add Biscuit's photo and a description, then upload two neighbour clips: a dog park and a doorbell. SAM 3.1 tracks every animal in each one.
Each clip goes onto a Cloudflare queue. The Worker sends it to SAM 3.1, then Muse Spark compares every tracked animal with Biscuit's photo. This is the real request and response.
Biscuit ranks first, with Spark's reasons. I confirm her, and Spark's tool loop writes a search plan and calls Muse Image for a poster. Reloading proves it's stored.
Under the hood: a React app, a Cloudflare Worker, D1 for state, R2 for media, and a queue for tracking. Our key decision: the owner confirms every match, never the model.
These are real runs: unit tests, an end-to-end test, and a benchmark on real footage where the right dog ranked first nine times out of nine.
Edge case: someone with only the share link tries to confirm a sighting. The server refuses with a 403, and nothing changes.
The evidence is in the repo. This is Find My Dog.
